headline: Data Centers Pay More for Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill shifts the costs of increasing electric generating capacity and distribution infrastructure to large energy users, primarily data centers, to prevent these costs from being passed on to residential customers.
status: Last Action: Approved by Governor-Chapter 1123 (effective 7/1/2026) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, customer advocates, Del. Destiny LeVere Bolling, Sen. L. Louise Lucas.
opponents: Data center industry, critics of Governor's amendments.
news_headline: Governor signs bills shifting data center energy costs
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed HB 1393, which aims to shift energy infrastructure costs onto large energy users like data centers, rather than residential customers. The legislation also extends Virginia's underground power line program through early 2033.

headline: Data Centers Must Report Water Use
short_summary: This bill requires utilities to report the water consumption of data centers, increasing transparency for communities regarding local resource use.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Sen. Kannan Srinivasan, environmental advocates, communities concerned about water usage.
opponents: Not explicitly stated in provided snippets.
news_headline: Data Center Bills Led 2026 Virginia General Assembly
news_summary: SB 553 mandates utilities report data center water consumption, providing communities with clearer insight into local resource use. This bill is part of a legislative focus on regulating Virginia's growing data center industry.

headline: New Siting Rules for Data Centers
short_summary: This bill establishes a new permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise and other environmental impacts before zoning approval.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Del. Joshua Thomas, communities concerned about noise and environmental impacts, lawmakers seeking stronger regulations.
opponents: Not explicitly stated in provided snippets.
news_headline: Data Center Siting Restrictions Passed in Virginia
news_summary: HB 153 creates a new permit process for high energy use facilities, mandating site assessments for noise near homes and schools. Localities can also require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
